working_title: Scotland's North-East Golf Coast: A Practical Guide to Playing Aberdeenshire
angle: Aberdeenshire is often overshadowed by the Fife and Ayrshire pilgrimages, but it offers one of the most concentrated and varied links rosters in Scotland. The post makes the case for Aberdeenshire as a self-contained golf trip, walking through the headline courses and a handful of quieter, cheaper options, with practical logistics for a visitor travelling from elsewhere in the UK.
research_notes:
- The region has more than 50 courses, ranging from classic seaside links to inland parkland. Royal Aberdeen (Balgownie) was founded in 1780, making it the sixth oldest golf club in the world. The Balgownie front nine is routinely cited among the finest in world golf.
- Cruden Bay, 25 miles north of Aberdeen, was designed by Tom Simpson and Herbert Fowler in 1926 and uses the enormous natural dunes of the Bay of Cruden. It holds a World Top 100 ranking. Has multiple blind shots and quirky angles. Weekend visitor windows can be restricted; shoulder-season weekdays (May, September) cited as best value.
- Murcar Links: classic stretch of links land with huge sand dunes, crumpled fairways, whins, burns and heather; ranked No. 30 in 2025 Top 100 Scottish Golf Courses. Shares the same dune system as Royal Aberdeen and is approximately four minutes' drive from Royal Aberdeen's car park. Originally laid out in 1909 with advice from Archie Simpson.
- Trump International (Menie Estate, Balmedie): Hawtree 2012 design, 7,428 yards, 16km north of Aberdeen. Has hosted DP World Tour's Scottish Championship from 2025. A new second course (Trump New Course) opened July 2025, designed by Martin Hawtree, Christian Lundin and Christine Fraser; named World's Best Golf Course 2025 by the World Golf Awards.
- Fraserburgh Golf Club: founded 1777, present course opened 1891, redesigned by James Braid in 1922.
- Royal Tarlair: noted as a long drive (55 mins from Aberdeen) but its 13th hole is a highlight; described as very affordable.
- Newburgh Links and Stonehaven also mentioned as quieter, value options along the coast.
- Practical logistics: car is essential for combining multiple courses; train from Edinburgh to Aberdeen takes approximately 2.5 hours, then car hire needed. Stay in or around Aberdeen city for easy access to Royal Aberdeen, Murcar, and Trump; Cruden Bay is a further 35 minutes north. Best travel window: late spring to early autumn for longer daylight and better conditions.
- Off-course: Aberdeen Beach, coastal walks (e.g. Slains Castle near Cruden Bay), whisky distilleries, castle trail, fishing towns.
